notes: Web 446 — SHADOW-POISON-NOV12 (Nov 12, 2026; layers on web 445). Owner evidence: today's fuel entry (Mobil Westwinds, 63.370 L, $133.65, odo 172,903, receipt attached) was created and verified in the Fuel list TWICE and vanished TWICE — the second creation re-verified in the list WITH its photo after Retry sync reported 'All synced · 5:43 PM'; forty minutes later a fresh check found 66 fill-ups again, the entry nowhere, the cloud copy at 66 records, 'Last backup try — landed ✓', 'All synced'; several other recent entries' receipt thumbnails were broken in the same lists. ROOT (bench-proven against the shipped sync code, not a story): js/cloudsync.js' lsSetRaw swallowed EVERY localStorage failure, and the record-list pull settled the key and advanced the per-key shadow (km.sh — 'the records this device holds') from the merged value it had merely TRIED to write, never verifying the write landed. Replay: a healthy surface lands the new fill in the cloud; the owner's phone — whose store sits at the quota wall (the whole web 441 saga: photo sheds, broken thumbnails) — pulls; the merged-book write silently fails, yet the meta persists SETTLED with the shadow naming the new fill; the phone's next flush reads 'in my shadow, absent from my book, present in the cloud' — the deliberate-delete signature — and authors the fill's deletion plus a sticky tombstone. The entry dies on every surface while every surface reports All synced. The first loss is the same family: a creation whose store never durably held it, certified as synced by its own window. FIX (js/cloudsync.js + modules/fuel.js): (1) verified writes — the record-list pull persists the merged book through lsSetVerified (set + read-back compare); a refused write leaves the local book standing, the shadow un-advanced, and the key DIRTY (never settled), so the flush pushes the union UP from the cloud's own copy and the status stays honest; the push's teaching write is verified the same way. (2) The delete-authoring basis (km.shb): a pending delete may only be read from a record this device PROVABLY held — in the shadow AND in the basis (the identities of the local list as last verified persisted under the shadow, plus deletes this device itself authored), absent locally, present in the cloud; a legacy meta with no basis is seeded from the book the device demonstrably holds at first sight, intersected with the shadow, so an inherited poisoned shadow is defused by the upgrade itself (a delete made before any basis existed may need one repeat — visible and recoverable, never silent loss). (3) Fuel records get a durable home: syncFillDocs maintains a per-record document in the account's fuel collection for EVERY fill (the stable key the v350 photo documents already use), written at the one verified-save door all fill writes pass through, and deleted when the fill leaves the book — a deliberate delete removes its document too; healMissingFills (once per session, at Fuel open) restores into the book any documented fill that is in NEITHER the local NOR the cloud book, revoking exactly its tombstone through the new CloudSync.reviveRecord — a surviving document is the proof the record was wiped, not deleted. En route, srcFromFuelDoc now distinguishes a document key from a record's own id (FB.loadDocs merges the key first, and a stored record's id field wins), so a restored fill keeps the identity its tombstone is addressed by. The broken thumbnails are the same wall: merged books carrying photos could not be written locally, so records kept arriving photo-less on the phone (the v350 graft heals them when it can; the wall itself is the phone's storage, unchanged).
